samples.question: This image shows one side view of a two-wheeled machine standing on a drawn ground line. The two wheels are the black rings with black spokes and a black hub; the frame, saddle and handlebar are coloured, the ground line is coloured, and the grey page border, the four grey corner ticks and the loose coloured spots near the top are fixed decoration that never indicates the answer. THE LEFT WHEEL is the wheel whose centre is further to the left of the page and THE RIGHT WHEEL is the other one, whichever end the handlebar happens to be drawn on; the machine faces left in some images and right in others, and that has nothing to do with the answer. A wheel's SIZE is the diameter of its black ring, measured across the ring from outer edge to outer edge. Compare the two diameters using this rule: if they differ by LESS than a tenth of the larger diameter, the wheels count as the same size; otherwise the wheel with the larger diameter is the larger one. No image in this set is a borderline case: the difference is always either well inside or well outside that tenth. The two wheels may be equal or one may be larger, the wheels change scale from image to image, and so do the frame colour, the spoke count, the number of spots and the facing direction. Judge the wheels drawn in this image, and do not answer from how the wheels of a bicycle usually compare. Which wheel is larger? Answer exactly one of: left, right, same.
